title: Sequence-aware kernel broker with confidence-weighted warmstarts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Kernel selection currently relies on static heuristics and occasional offline profiling. For mixed workloads (short chat turns + long-document summarization) and across heterogeneous GPU fleets, static rules either over-hedge (higher cost) or under-fit (latency SLO breaches).

Proposal: Implement a lightweight "kernel broker" runtime component that: 1) collects a short running window of per-request sequence-length features and microprobe latency samples; 2) maintains a per-architecture + model fingerprint table with confidence scores for candidate kernels; 3) uses a confidence-weighted warmstart policy to pick an initial kernel, optionally run a short microbenchmark probe for ambiguous cases, and fall back deterministically on safety thresholds.

Key innovations vs. existing approaches: confidence-weighted decisions (not pure bandit), explicit short-horizon sequence-length forecasting to bias kernel choice for expected token distribution, and warmstart microprobes that cost a bounded token budget to reduce long-tail latency risk. This aims to improve 95th/99th percentile latency on mixed loads while preserving unit cost savings from cheaper kernels where safe.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes broker config toggles (enabled/disabled, probe budget, confidence threshold) via config service
95th percentile tail latency reduced by >=10% on mixed test workload compared to current static heuristics
Per-token cost neutral or better for at least 70% of observed workload profiles (no regression >5% for critical customers)
Canary rollout plan documented and implemented with automatic rollback on latency SLO violation
Telemetry surface: per-request kernel choice, confidence score, probe outcome, and decision latency visible in Console
technical_notes: Broker state: small LRU table keyed by (model-version, arch-fingerprint, recent-seqlen-bucket) -> {kernel-id, score, last-sampled}
Confidence update rule: exponential smoothing of microprobe reward (latency + cost) with decay tuned per-customer SLA tier

Probe design: prefill/early-decode microprobe limited to first N tokens or M ms, uses a cheap kernel to measure decode path and kv-cache perf; probe budget per-request set to 0.5% token overhead default
Safety policy: if decision latency + expected decode latency > latency SLO or confidence < threshold, choose a conservative kernel with known latency bound
Fallbacks: deterministic fallback map for archival models and unsupported kernels; telemetry flag to capture missing kernel compatibility events
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design doc + config schema (owners: Marcus Li, Olivia Nguyen). Deliverable: confluence/design-kernel-broker (link below)
Week 2: Broker runtime stub + microprobe harness in serving runtime; minimal per-request hook for seqlen histogram sampling
Week 3: Integrate broker with offline kernel-performance store and implement confidence updater; basic Console telemetry emitted
Week 4: Run synthetic benchmarks and customer-mirroring load tests (short/chat vs long/doc mixes); iterate thresholds
Week 5: Canary on Dedicated pool, monitor 95/99p latencies, iterate. If stable, schedule wider rollout in runtime-1.20
